---
title: quarto-graph
type: moc
---

`quarto-graph` enables using **Wikilinks** in a quarto website, where pages are
connected via links. Wikilinks can expediate knowledge discovery, because 
connections can be explicitly captured and presented to your audience. This site itself was built with `quarto-graph`.

This project was heavily inspired by [Obsidian](https://obsidian.md/help/), a note-taking app that lets you visualize your personal notes as a giant graph. Wikilinks, or more generally analyzing connected concepts using graphs, have a long history in various domains [^examples]. `quarto-graph`'s goal is bringing this feature to your quarto-powered websites.

[^examples]: [Connected Papers](https://www.connectedpapers.com/) is a website that lets you explore connected papers using graphs. [Six Degrees of Wikipedia](https://www.sixdegreesofwikipedia.com/) allows you to explore wikipedia by finding the shortest path between pages.

`quarto-graph` grants powerful navigational features. For example, with [[The Graph Widget]], users can see how different pages are connected in a graph, and they can click on a node, which will take them to that specific page.

{{< quarto-graph-full >}}

In the graph,

- All pages are *nodes*
- Connections are pages that link to the current page, or that link from current page to other pages. Links can either be Wikilinks using the square brackets syntax e.g. `[[Getting Started]]`, or regular markdown links e.g. [`[Getting Started](getting-started/index.qmd)`](getting-started/index.qmd).

In addition to the graph widget, wikilinks allow us to auto-generate 
[[Backlinks]], scroll to the end of this page to see all the pages that 
reference the current page.
